heading: Looking for a HomeCourt video workflow?
text: Explore how basketball training records, auto clipping and Shot Tracer fit different tasks. Our independent HomeCourt guides cover choosing a workflow, checking a recording and turning a playable export into clips.

heading: Have a HomeCourt workout recording?
text: If your HomeCourt session offers a video export, first save and replay that file outside the app. Then review which basketball moments belong in a highlight. This prepared demo shows clip selection; it does not connect to HomeCourt, import an account or process your video in the browser.
links: Prepare a HomeCourt video for editing

heading: HomeCourt shot analysis and Shot Tracer
text: A shot-analysis metric and a visible ball-flight trail answer different questions. Use this demo to explore the appearance of a trajectory effect. Do not treat the drawn trail as a measured release angle or as a replacement for a complete basketball practice record.

heading: Starting with a HomeCourt video export
text: Keep the playable source export before making selections. Check its crop, overlays and the beginning and ending of each play, then record timestamps for your shortlist. Keep a complete training record separately: a reel of selected makes cannot represent the shooting percentage of the whole workout.
links: Check a HomeCourt export before editing

heading: Adding a tracer to training footage
text: If you are comparing this effect with HomeCourt shot analysis, distinguish presentation from measurement. Keep an unedited copy and inspect the basketball flight at normal playback speed. A line added to the video is not, on its own, a calibrated release-angle measurement.
links: Compare HomeCourt metrics and Shot Tracer

heading: Planning a HomeCourt recording session
text: Before a full workout, make a short recording and inspect the saved result. Note the phone position and check that the activity stays in view. If reception is unreliable, confirm what the app can record offline and verify upload and playback afterwards instead of assuming a visible score guarantees a saved video.
links: Use the HomeCourt camera setup checklist

heading: A HomeCourt practice setup is a specific use case
text: Framing one basketball shooting activity differs from covering a moving full-court game. Check the whole area of action you intend to record and keep equipment outside active play. Our HomeCourt setup guide focuses on a repeatable practice view, with an editable diagram for planning camera and player positions.
links: Plan a HomeCourt practice camera position

heading: Plan a HomeCourt camera setup on the diagram
text: Mark a proposed phone position and the shooting spots you want to include. Take the drawing to practice and verify the actual phone view before recording. The camera marker is a planning note; it does not simulate a lens, certify a safe placement or configure HomeCourt.

heading: Keep a manual record alongside HomeCourt
text: Use this chart to log your own observations when reviewing a HomeCourt workout or when you prefer manual entry. Enter every attempt rather than only highlights, and mark uncertain locations honestly. This browser chart does not edit HomeCourt sessions, synchronise accounts or automatically detect basketball shots.

heading: Organize a HomeCourt workout export
text: Once you have a playable video file, use the timestamp log to identify each basketball clip, its player and its context. Keep the source file unchanged and review your selection before sharing. The worksheet organizes editing notes; it does not export a HomeCourt account or recover missing recordings.
